title: Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Properties of Child and Parent Versions of the Pediatric Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit
text_snippet: Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Properties of Child and Parent Versions of the Pediatric Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit Introduction: Both clinicians and researchers recognize the importance of the individual’s perspective when evaluating the effectiveness of healthcare interventions in real-world settings. Self-report scales are a commonly used measurement tool that allows individuals to assess their own experiences and perceptions, enabling them to make subjective judgements about specific variables. Since auditory perception is directly related to the hearing process, self-reports play a critical role in hearing assessments. This study aimed to adapt the Pediatric Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit (P-APHAB) into Turkish and to evaluate its validity and reliability for children with hearing loss and their parents.Method: A total of 359 children (220 with normal hearing and 139 with hearing loss) and 359 parents participated in the study. Both child and parent versions of the scale were administered. The original scale was translated into Turkish as part of the cultural adaptation process and converted from a 7-point Likert scale to a 5-point Likert scale to ensure its suitability for children's cognitive level. title: The Effect of a Social-Emotional Learning-Based Intervention Program on the Social-Emotional Skills of Gifted Elementary School Students
text_snippet: The Effect of a Social-Emotional Learning-Based Intervention Program on the Social-Emotional Skills of Gifted Elementary School Students Introduction: In recent years, social-emotional learning has emerged as a key educational approach that supports students’ emotional, social, and behavioral competencies in addition to their academic development. In particular, systematically addressing the social-emotional needs of gifted students alongside their cognitive development is of critical importance for their holistic development. Despite their high cognitive potential, gifted elementary school students may require systematic support in areas such as self-regulation, social relationships, self-confidence, and impulse control. In this context, it is important to experimentally examine the effectiveness of structured intervention programs based on social-emotional learning.Method: This study examined the effectiveness of a social-emotional learning-based intervention program for gifted elementary school students. The research was conducted using an experimental design with an experimental and control group, including pretest, posttest, and follow-up measurements. title: Relationship between Bullying and Theory of Mind in School-Aged Children with Stuttering
text_snippet: Relationship between Bullying and Theory of Mind in School-Aged Children with Stuttering Introduction: Children who stutter are more likely to experience peer bullying which may negatively affect their theory of mind development. This study aimed to investigate the relationships between stuttering severity, exposure to peer bullying and theory of mind abilities in children aged 6 to 9 years who stutter. Additionally, it examined whether the levels of peer bullying experienced by these children differed according to demographic variables such as age, gender and parental education level.Method: A total of 39 children who stutter were included in the study. The participants were divided into two age groups: 6-7 years and 8-9 years. Stuttering severity was assessed using the Turkish version of the Stuttering Severity Instrument-Fourth Edition (SSI-4-TR), while exposure to peer bullying was evaluated using the Peer Bullying Questionnaire. Age and developmentally appropriate tasks were used to assess theory of mind abilities. Accordingly, second-order false-belief tasks were administered to children aged 6-7 years, whereas advanced theory of mind tasks were administered to children aged 8-9 years. title: The Role of Sustainable Leadership in the Relationship Between Organizational Identification and Teacher Entrepreneurship Among Special Education Teachers
text_snippet: The Role of Sustainable Leadership in the Relationship Between Organizational Identification and Teacher Entrepreneurship Among Special Education Teachers Introduction: This study examined the mediating role of perceived sustainable leadership of school principals in the relationship between organizational identification and teachers' entrepreneurial behavior among special education teachers.Method: The study employed a correlational research design, and the mediation relationships were tested using Structural Equation Modeling. The study sample consisted of 478 teachers working in special education schools, rehabilitation centers, guidance and research centers, and inclusive education settings across different provinces of Türkiye. Data were collected using the Organizational Identification Scale, the Sustainable Leadership Scale, and the Entrepreneurial Teacher Behaviors Scale.Findings: The findings indicated that organizational identification was positively and directly associated with entrepreneurial teacher behaviors. Organizational identification was also significantly associated with perceived sustainable leadership behaviors, and sustainable leadership demonstrated a significant relationship with entrepreneurial teacher behaviors. title: Competencies of Special Education Teachers in Preparing Students with Developmental Disabilities for Independent Living
text_snippet: Competencies of Special Education Teachers in Preparing Students with Developmental Disabilities for Independent Living Introduction: Independent living skills are the skills necessary for individuals to sustain their daily lives as independent adults and members of society. These skills include daily living skills such as self-care, food preparation, and personal hygiene; personal skills that facilitate communication with others; and skills for managing financial resources. This study aims to determine the competency levels of special education teachers in preparing students with developmental disabilities for independent living.Method: A descriptive research model, one of the quantitative research methods, was used to determine the teachers’ target competency levels. The study included 227 special education teachers currently working in public schools and special education and rehabilitation centers under the Ministry of National Education. Research data were collected using a questionnaire developed by the researchers based on relevant literature and the opinions of field experts, and subsequently analyzed descriptively by the researchers.Findings: Data regarding four areas of independent living skills were collected and analyzed in the study. title: Global Citizenship Levels and Perceptions of Global and National Citizenship Among Gifted Students in the 21st Century
text_snippet: Global Citizenship Levels and Perceptions of Global and National Citizenship Among Gifted Students in the 21st Century Introduction: Building a sustainable future requires individuals to assume responsibilities not only toward their own countries but also toward the world. This study aims to determine gifted students’ levels of global citizenship and their perceptions of global and national citizenship, given their potential to shape the future of their countries and the world.Method: A concurrent transformational mixed-methods design was employed. Participants were selected through criterion sampling. Quantitative data were collected from 70 gifted students and qualitative data from 24. Data were gathered using the Global Citizenship Scale and a semi- structured interview form.Findings: Gifted students demonstrated moderate levels of global citizenship, with scores differing significantly according to the SAC they attended. Students predominantly described citizenship of the Republic of Türkiye as a source of pride, while some identified themselves as global citizens. A substantial proportion indicated that they might live abroad in the future for various reasons. title: Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis of Research on Social Studies Education for Students with Special Needs (2000-2024)
text_snippet: Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis of Research on Social Studies Education for Students with Special Needs (2000-2024) Introduction: Social studies education for students with special needs has become an increasingly important field of research as inclusive education advances. However, the temporal development of scientific production, prominent actors, and collaboration structures in this field have not been investigated comprehensively. This study aims to reveal the structural and trend-related characteristics of the field by analyzing the bibliometric properties of research published in this domain.Method: This study was a review based on bibliometric analysis. Publications indexed in the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection and published between 2000 and 2024 were included in the analysis. The literature search was conducted on March 19, 2025. Bibliometric analyses were carried out using the Bibliometrix package and VOSviewer software. Publication and citation trends, as well as country, institution, and author productivity and collaboration networks, were examined.Findings: The findings indicate a significant increase in publications over the past decade and reveal that scientific output is concentrated within a relatively small set of countries, institutions, and authors. title: Effectiveness of Adapted Physical Activity for Teaching Colour Concept Skills to Children with Autism
text_snippet: Effectiveness of Adapted Physical Activity for Teaching Colour Concept Skills to Children with Autism Introduction: This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of adapted physical activity in teaching colour concept skills to children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.Method: A multiple-baseline across participants design, a type of single-subject research method, was employed. The study was conducted with three children with autism aged between 3 and 6 years. The intervention was delivered one-to-one in a structured setting; follow-up and generalisation sessions were planned following the teaching process. Follow-up data were collected in the first, third and fourth weeks following the completion of the teaching. Generalisation sessions were conducted with different personnel, settings and time arrangements.Findings: The findings showed that the participants acquired colour concept skills. Participants maintained the skills they had acquired during the follow-up sessions held in the first, third and fourth weeks following the instruction. It was determined that the skills could be generalised across different people, settings, materials and time conditions. title: The Effectiveness of a Home Visiting Program on Skill Acquisition for Mothers of Young Children with Special Needs
text_snippet: The Effectiveness of a Home Visiting Program on Skill Acquisition for Mothers of Young Children with Special Needs Introduction: Home-visiting one of the family-centered approaches—involves specialists systematically visiting families in their homes to support their children’s development and education. A review of the literature reveals that research on home-visiting in Türkiye is limited, and the necessity for this study arises from the need to identify the potential effects of home-visiting on families and their children. In this context, the aim of the study is to enable mothers of children with special needs to teach their children daily living skills through strategies implemented during home-visiting, and to ensure that their children acquire, maintain, and generalize these skills.Method: The participants comprised four children aged four to six diagnosed with Down syndrome and their mothers. The study employed a multiple-probe design across behaviors, a rigorous single-subject research methodology. The home-visiting program was implemented over a 16-week period. title: An Examination of Special Education Life Studies and Social Skills Textbooks within the Framework of the TYMM
text_snippet: An Examination of Special Education Life Studies and Social Skills Textbooks within the Framework of the TYMM Introduction: This study aims to conduct a comparative examination of the primary-level Special Education Social Skills (SS) and Life Studies (LS) textbooks within the scope of the Virtue–Value–Action Model Framework of the Century of Türkiye Education Model (TYMM).Method: A descriptive content analysis was employed within a qualitative research design. Texts, instructions, dialogues, and visuals were coded as “meaningful content units.” The coding scheme, based on the 20 values and value indicators in the TYMM, was validated through expert opinion and verified through repeated readings.Findings: Of the 1331 references, 76.4% were located in the LS textbook (n = 1017) and 23.6% in the SS textbook (n = 314). The most frequently emphasised values were Responsibility (n = 230), Diligence (n = 196), and Respect (n = 161). Within the theme of “Liveable Environment,” the indicators “having disaster awareness” and “attaching importance to environmental cleanliness and sustainability” remained limited (n = 14). title: Investigating the Performance Practices of Musically Gifted Individuals with Autism in Professional Music Recording Environments
text_snippet: Investigating the Performance Practices of Musically Gifted Individuals with Autism in Professional Music Recording Environments Introduction: This study aims to examine the musical performance practices of individuals with autism in professional music studio environments. The research is guided by the question: “What factors are observed in the performance practices of individuals with autism in professional music studio recordings?” By exploring the experiences of individuals with autism throughout the studio recording process in depth, the study seeks to address gaps in the literature and provide findings that can inform practice. In doing so, it aims to contribute to making music production environments more inclusive and accessible.Method: The study is based on semi-structured interviews conducted with the families, educators, and tonmeisters of individuals with autism, researcher observations, and descriptive analyses of video recordings captured during studio sessions.Findings: The findings indicate that individuals with autism require guidance during the recording process; that tonmeisters should adopt patient and understanding approaches; that prior interaction with families facilitates communication; and that studio environments should be designed in accordance with the specific needs of these indi

title: Activity-Based Number Teaching for Students with Learning Disabilities: A Multi-Case Study
text_snippet: Activity-Based Number Teaching for Students with Learning Disabilities: A Multi-Case Study Introduction: Introduction: Recently, interdisciplinary approaches have gained increasing importance in mathematics education, and the contribution of music to the learning process has attracted increasing attention. However, there is limited evidence regarding the effects of music-based practices on students with learning disabilities (LD). This study examined reflections on activity-based number instruction within the context of Orff music pedagogy (OMP) among primary school students with LD.Method: This study used a multiple-case study design and qualitative research methods. Eight students, selected through criterion sampling, participated in the study at a primary school located in a city center. During the data collection process, semi-structured interviews, observations, and document analyses were conducted. Activity evaluation forms and worksheets were also utilized. The implementation was carried out by researchers in the support education room and music and drama halls. Four activities were implemented over 4 weeks, comprising 24 lesson hours. title: Effects of Shaping Procedures on Cooperative Behavior During Haircut Routines in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
text_snippet: Effects of Shaping Procedures on Cooperative Behavior During Haircut Routines in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Introduction: Haircuts are essential for social acceptance, personal care, and hygiene. However, many children with autism spectrum disorder experience substantial difficulty during haircuts and may exhibit problem behaviors such as aggression, self-injury, and escape attempts. The present study examines the effectiveness of a shaping procedure for increasing cooperation during haircuts in children with autism spectrum disorder.Method: Three boys diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder participated in this study. A 16-step haircut procedure was systematically taught using a changing criterion design embedded within a multiple baseline across participants design. In addition, parents’ views on the intervention process and outcomes were collected through semi-structured interviews, and the social validity of the study was evaluated.Findings: The findings indicated a significant improvement in cooperation-based behaviors, and all participants successfully completed the haircut procedure at the end of the intervention. title: An Investigation of the Effectiveness of Music and Rhythm Activities Presented Using the Direct Instruction Method in Teaching Rhythmic Counting Skills to Individuals with Special Needs
text_snippet: An Investigation of the Effectiveness of Music and Rhythm Activities Presented Using the Direct Instruction Method in Teaching Rhythmic Counting Skills to Individuals with Special Needs Introduction: The primary goal of special education services is to support independent living skills of individuals with special needs. Functional academic skills are essential for daily living and independence. Counting skills are important as they are frequently used in daily life and form the basis for advanced mathematics. Teaching mathematics to individuals with intellectual disabilities requires structured and evidence-based methods. Music and rhythm activities are considered to support attention, motivation, and learning. This study examined the effectiveness of music and rhythm activities delivered through direct instruction in teaching rhythmic counting skills to students with intellectual disabilities in school settings.Method: Participants were students aged 14-15 with intellectual disabilities. A multiple-probe design across participants, a single-subject design, was used. Rhythmic counting skills were taught using songs and rhythm sticks through music and rhythm activities based on direct instruction. title: Spatial Accessibility Audit and Improvement Plan for the Bingöl University Campus
text_snippet: Spatial Accessibility Audit and Improvement Plan for the Bingöl University Campus Introduction: Physical barriers on university campuses restrict the independent mobility and full participation of individuals with disabilities, violating fundamental rights and global accessibility standards. This study evaluates the compliance of Bingöl University’s central campus with national and international accessibility criteria, identifying critical infrastructural deficiencies and proposing targeted, standards-based improvements.Method: The spatial accessibility of the campus was assessed through systematic on-site observations and technical document reviews. The methodological framework centered on a rigorous field evaluation of outdoor spaces and indoor facilities. Key areas -including circulation pathways, ramps, parking lots, wayfinding elements, building entrances, corridors, classrooms, laboratories, and sanitary facilities- were examined using structured checklists, spatial measurements, and photographic documentation. These empirical findings were cross-referenced with campus master plans and architectural blueprints to assess compliance with accessibility norms. title: Gifted but Left Behind: Socioeconomic Barriers Facing Disadvantaged Gifted Children in Türkiye
text_snippet: Gifted but Left Behind: Socioeconomic Barriers Facing Disadvantaged Gifted Children in Türkiye Introduction: This study examines the barriers faced by gifted children from socioeconomically disadvantaged families in Türkiye in gaining access to specialized talent development programs, specifically Science and Art Centers (BILSEM). Bronfenbrenner’s ecological systems theory provides the theoretical framework for understanding the multilayered challenges within children's environments.Method: In this study, we used a qualitative research design and conducted a reflexive thematic analysis. We collected data through semi-structured interviews with seven BILSEM teachers, seven classroom teachers, ten school counselors, and eight school principals working in schools serving low socio-economic communities.Results: The findings revealed that families have the most significant influence on children's participation in BILSEM, followed by factors related to the child, school, and teacher roles, as well as the structural attributes of BILSEM. title: Analysis of Studies on Mathematics Learning Disabilities Through Document Analysis
text_snippet: Analysis of Studies on Mathematics Learning Disabilities Through Document Analysis Introduction: This study examined studies on mathematics learning disabilities conducted in our country between 2002 and 2022.Method: The study employs document analysis. In line with the specified purpose, a field search was conducted in the Council of Higher Education Thesis Center, TR Index, ERIC, and EBSCO databases. The dataset comprised master's theses (n = 17), doctoral theses (n = 10) and articles (n = 22). The obtained data were analyzed using descriptive and content analysis techniques.Findings: According to the research findings, it was determined that studies on mathematics learning difficulties have increased especially since 2014, and the most intense publication year was 2019. It was determined that the number of articles was higher than the theses, and in terms of method, both qualitative and quantitative research designs were frequently preferred. It is noteworthy that the most commonly used data collection tool in studies is interview, and the participant group is generally primary school students between the ages of 5-10.The studies in the data set were have been classified in detail concerning findings, results, and recommendations. title: Interactive Book Reading Scale for Children Who Are Deaf or Hard of Hearing-Mother Form: A Scale Development Study
text_snippet: Interactive Book Reading Scale for Children Who Are Deaf or Hard of Hearing-Mother Form: A Scale Development Study Introduction: This study sought to develop a psychometrically sound instrument for assessing the knowledge and awareness of mothers of children aged 2-6 years with hearing loss regarding interactive book reading.Method: The sample consisted of 270 mothers of children with hearing loss living in Ankara. An initial pool of 52 items was drafted on the basis of a literature review and a focus group interview conducted with 10 mothers. After expert appraisal, the pool was reduced to 31 items. A preliminary administration with 10 mothers was carried out to check the clarity of the items, and the main pilot application was then conducted with 250 mothers. The sample was split at random into two groups of 125, with one used for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and the other for Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA).Findings: The EFA produced a theoretically meaningful and statistically sound three-factor solution comprising 26 items: General Attitudes Toward Reading, Developmental Effects, and Interactive Reading Behaviors. title: Problem Behaviors Displayed by Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder in Educational Settings: A Prevalence Study
text_snippet: Problem Behaviors Displayed by Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder in Educational Settings: A Prevalence Study Introduction: Problem behaviors are defined as patterns of behavior that cause harm to the individual or others, create limitations in social and academic domains, and persist in ways that are contrary to cultural norms. Risks related to problem behaviors are identified through prevalence studies, which also provide guidance for intervention planning. In Türkiye, aside from one study conducted with parents, there are no prevalence studies in educational settings. The aim of this study is to determine the prevalence and risk factors of problem behaviors exhibited by individuals with ASD in educational settings in Türkiye and to determine teachers’ levels of difficulty in responding to these behaviors.Method: This study utilized a descriptive correlational survey design. Data were obtained from 981 students diagnosed with ASD using the Problem Behavior Inventory-Short Form. The ages of the students ranged from 2 to 18; 223 were female, and 758 were male. Teachers’ levels of difficulty were determined using the Autism Problem Behaviors Teacher Form with 491 teachers. ASD severity was also measured using the Adapted Autism Behavior Checklist.Findings: The prevalence of problem behavior

title: Theory of Mind, Pragmatic Language, and Emotion Processing in Autism Spectrum Disorder and Specific Learning Disorder
text_snippet: Theory of Mind, Pragmatic Language, and Emotion Processing in Autism Spectrum Disorder and Specific Learning Disorder Introduction: The current study investigated theory of mind (ToM), pragmatic language, and emotion processing skills in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and special learning disorder (SLD).Method: The study was conducted using a correlational survey design. The study group comprised individuals with ASD (14) and SLD (13), and typically developing (TD) individuals (13) aged between 8 and 12. The research data were collected using a Personal Information Form, the PEABODY Picture Vocabulary Test, First- and Second-Order ToM Tests, Reading the Mind in the Eyes Test (RMET)-Children’s Version (6-16), Pragmatic Language Skills Inventory (PLSI), and the Test of Perception of Affect via Nonverbal Cues (TPANC).Findings: According to the findings from the study, the ASD group displayed the lowest performance in all receptive language, ToM, emotion processing, and pragmatic language skills. title: Exploring the Professional Experiences of Teachers in Special Education Institutions: Challenges and Adaptation
text_snippet: Exploring the Professional Experiences of Teachers in Special Education Institutions: Challenges and Adaptation Introduction: The student profiles in special education institutions may differ significantly from those in mainstream educational settings. Educators working with students with special needs face unique challenges not commonly experienced by general education teachers. Previous research emphasizes that teaching in special education involves distinct professional experiences and difficulties.Method: This study employed a qualitative research design with a phenomenological approach to explore the professional experiences of special education teachers in depth. The participants included 19 teachers working at a special education institution. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using a thematic analysis. Emerging themes, sub-themes, and codes were identified and interpreted accordingly.Findings: The findings revealed that participants faced multidimensional challenges in the educational process. Students' learning difficulties and deficiencies in basic skills necessitate that teachers to simultaneously fulfill both academic and counseling roles. title: Opinions of Physical Education and Sports Teachers Working in Special Education Schools About Their Lessons
text_snippet: Opinions of Physical Education and Sports Teachers Working in Special Education Schools About Their Lessons Introduction: The aim of this research is to examine the opinions of physical education and sports teachers working in special education schools regarding sports and physical activities lessons.Method: A phenomenological design was employed using a qualitative research approach. Data collected through semi-structured interviews were analyzed through coding and themes. During the analysis process, the interview questions were examined separately, codes were generated from each participant’s responses, and themes were derived from these codes in accordance with an inductive approach. Seven teachers participated in the study.Findings: Teachers’ statements were evaluated under three main categories. (i) Within the scope of opinions on the course, teachers emphasized that sports and physical activity lessons make a significant contribution to student development, that the weekly hours allocated to these lessons are insufficient, that they face challenges in implementing the curriculum, and that they employ various teaching methods and techniques to keep students active during the lessons. title: Knowledge, Beliefs, and Practice: A Multidisciplinary Perspective on Applied Behavior Analysis and Naturalistic Teaching Approaches
text_snippet: Knowledge, Beliefs, and Practice: A Multidisciplinary Perspective on Applied Behavior Analysis and Naturalistic Teaching Approaches Introduction: This study aimed to explore the views and experiences of professionals involved in intervention processes for individuals with special needs regarding practices based on Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA). In the Turkish context, ABA is often referred to as Uygulamalı Davranış Analizi (UDA[ABATR]); however, in recent years, these terms have sometimes been treated as if they represent distinct disciplinary approaches, leading to conceptual confusion. The study also examined professionals’ perspectives on Naturalistic Teaching Approaches (NTA).Method: Designed as a qualitative case study, the research involved semi-structured interviews with 20 professionals who graduated from undergraduate programs in special education, early childhood education, child development, and speech and language therapy. The data were analyzed using content analysis.Findings: The findings of the current study show that professionals experience conceptual confusion regarding ABA, ABATR, and NTA-based practices. title: Experiences of Teachers Working with Students with Visual Impairments Regarding the Use of Assistive Technologies in Educational Activities
text_snippet: Experiences of Teachers Working with Students with Visual Impairments Regarding the Use of Assistive Technologies in Educational Activities Introduction: Assistive technologies utilized in education support equal opportunities by fostering the participation of individuals with special needs in learning processes. These technologies are pivotal for students with visual impairments, who experience greater difficulty accessing information than other student groups. In this research, we aim to examine teachers' experiences with assistive technologies for students with visual impairments.Method: We employed a qualitative research design, specifically a phenomenological approach. The research group comprised 14 special education teachers working at a school for the visually impaired. We collected data through semi-structured interviews, analyzed them using content analysis techniques, and determined Reliability.Findings: The research yielded nine themes from teachers' opinions. These themes were as follows: assistive technologies used; competence and frequency of use; methods of acquisition; training received; positive and negative experiences; needs; suggestions for improvement; and technologies they wish to learn. Participants declared that these technologies nurture the teaching process and support students' independence.

title: Investigation of Special Education Teachers' Awareness Levels Toward Early Childhood Special Education
text_snippet: Investigation of Special Education Teachers' Awareness Levels Toward Early Childhood Special Education Introduction: This study aimed to determine the awareness levels of special education teachers regarding early childhood special education services. In this context, teachers’ conceptual knowledge about early childhood special education (ECSE), their general perspectives toward this field, and their sensitivity to related processes were evaluated.Method: This descriptive survey study was conducted with special education teachers working in the province of Samsun, and data were collected from 432 teachers. The data were gathered using the Early Childhood Special Education Awareness Scale developed by the researcher, consisting of six factors.Findings: The findings revealed that special education teachers’ overall awareness levels regarding ECSE services were high. The highest mean was observed in the Individualized Education Planning and Collaboration dimension, whereas the lowest mean was found in the Perception of ECSE and Scientific Approach dimension. Regarding demographic variables, no significant differences were found. title: Customising ICT for Visually Impaired Learners in South African Full-Service Schools: Perspectives from Teachers
text_snippet: Customising ICT for Visually Impaired Learners in South African Full-Service Schools: Perspectives from Teachers Introduction: The study investigates teachers’ perspectives on the adaptation of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) for teaching visually impaired learners (VILs) in Full-Service schools (FSSs). By foregrounding these insights, the study seeks to contribute to the effective implementation of inclusive education (IE) for VILs in FSS across South Africa.Method: The study used a qualitative case study design grounded in an interpretive paradigm. A qualitative approach was used to obtain rich, detailed accounts of teachers’ experiences and viewpoints. Purposive sampling was applied to select participants, leading to four focus group discussions comprising five teachers each (20 in total). The collected data were examined through thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns and central ideas. The thematic analysis led to five themes to be discussed.Findings: Teachers expressed a clear readiness to adapt ICT for VILs, yet they were hindered by several barriers, including limited parental engagement, insufficient funding to procure ICT resources, the absence of reliable power sources, time constraints, and inadequate practical training. title: Problem Solving and Posing Processes of Middle School Students with Hearing Loss in Inclusive Education
text_snippet: Problem Solving and Posing Processes of Middle School Students with Hearing Loss in Inclusive Education Introduction: Problem-solving and problem-posing skills play a crucial role in developing mathematical thinking and connecting mathematics to real-world contexts. However, while existing research has predominantly focused on students with normal hearing, the experiences of students with hearing loss in these processes have not been sufficiently examined. In particular, the fact that there is a limited number of studies on problem-posing skills highlights the need for further research in this area.Method: The aim of this study was to examine the problem-solving processes and problem-posing skills of middle school students with hearing loss in inclusive classrooms when solving daily life problems requiring multiplication and division. A basic qualitative research design was adopted, and data were collected through semi-structured interviews. During the interviews, five problems that corresponded to the structures of equivalent groups, comparisons, sequences-fields, and combinations in multiplication and division operations were presented. title: Leadership at the Boundaries of Inclusion: Special Education School Principals' Perspectives on Inclusive Education Policies and Ethical Dilemmas
text_snippet: Leadership at the Boundaries of Inclusion: Special Education School Principals' Perspectives on Inclusive Education Policies and Ethical Dilemmas Introduction: Inclusive education, which has become a paradigm at the global level, has experienced a numerical expansion in Türkiye; however, the gap between policy and practice confronts school administrators with the management of complex ethical dilemmas. This study aims to contribute to the understanding of the policy–practice tension and to provide empirical data on managerial experiences that have been addressed in a limited manner in the literature, by examining the leadership, ethics, and organizational meaning dimensions of inclusive education from a holistic perspective. The primary purpose of the study is to reveal special education school principals' perceptions of inclusive education policies, how they make sense of these policies within their own contexts, and through which values and experiences they interpret the ethical dilemmas they encounter during the implementation process.Method: A phenomenological design, one of the qualitative research approaches, was adopted in the study. title: Bibliometric Analysis of Publications on Parents of Children with Special Needs
text_snippet: Bibliometric Analysis of Publications on Parents of Children with Special Needs Introduction: Children with special needs are individuals born with congenital or acquired physical, intellectual, sensory or behavioral differences. Since these children have different needs from other individuals in society, these differences affect their own lives and the lives of their families in different ways. This study aimed to reveal the future course of research on parents of children with special needs by examining the current situation and improvements in the field of special education, evaluating the scientific outputs of research on parents of children with special needs on a global scale.Method: Articles concerning the experiences of parents of children with special needs were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC), and bibliometric analyses were conducted using VOSviewer software. The analysis was based on research articles on “parents of children with special needs” discovered between January 1, 1990 and December 31, 2023 using all WOSCC indexes. title: Intervening in the Problem of Disproportionate Representation in the Identification of the Gifted: A Systematic Review Study
text_snippet: Intervening in the Problem of Disproportionate Representation in the Identification of the Gifted: A Systematic Review Study Introduction: Identification is a systematic selection process designed to enable gifted individuals access educational opportunities they need. Countries have their own unique gifted identification systems that they use to select these individuals for educational programs. However, despite many different intervention methods, due to socio-economic, racial, and regional factors some groups are still underrepresented or disproportionately overrepresented in the identification system. Solutions for these problems continues to be a current issue in the literature.Method: This study examined intervention methods that address disproportionate representation among groups that differ in key characteristics in gifted education, following the PRISMA method. To do so, we conducted a literature review between November 2024 and January 2025 using the Web of Science, Scopus, ERIC, ProQuest, TR Dizin, DergiPark, and YÖK Thesis databases.Findings: Although we imposed no year restrictions because of the narrow scope of the search, the retrieved studies spanned 1988–2024. title: Contributions of Musical Activities to the Development of the Verbal and Musical Expression Skills of Children with Special Needs
text_snippet: Contributions of Musical Activities to the Development of the Verbal and Musical Expression Skills of Children with Special Needs Introduction: This study investigates how play, dance, and music-based activities contribute to the development of verbal and musical expression skills in children with special needs. Although previous research highlights the positive influence of music, movement, and play on social and cognitive development, persistent challenges in verbal expression and motor coordination necessitate further inquiry.Method: Aqualitative descriptive case study was conducted with eight children diagnosed with mild intellectual disability, selected through typical case sampling. Data were collected across a 10-week program (800 minutes of instruction) using participant observations, structured checklists, and parental interviews. Weekly observation diaries supported the evaluation of in-class performance. Checklist items were refined and validated through expert review and the Lawshe content validity technique.Findings: Results indicated gradual improvements in both verbal and musical expression skills, with musical development advancing more rapidly due to the repetitive and engaging nature of music. title: Opinions of Special Education Teachers Working in Guidance and Research Centers on Functional Vision Assessment of Individuals with Low Vision
text_snippet: Opinions of Special Education Teachers Working in Guidance and Research Centers on Functional Vision Assessment of Individuals with Low Vision Introduction: In educational assessment processes, functional vision skills of individuals with low vision are assessed. Functional vision assessment provides critical insights into how, and to what extent, these individuals utilize their remaining visual capacity in daily life. The evaluation of functional vision skills plays a critical role in guiding the orientation, placement, and educational planning for individuals with low vision. These processes are primarily conducted within Guidance and Research Centers (GRC). This study examines the perspectives of special education teachers working in the GRCs regarding the functional vision assessment of individuals with low vision. Method: This study employed phenomenological design, a qualitative research method. The study group consisted of 16 special education teachers working in the GRCs. A semi-structured interview form was conducted as the data collection tool. The data obtained from the interviews were analyzed using content analysis.Findings: The researchers collected the special education teachers’ perception under five themes. title: Problems Faced by Child Development Specialists Working in Special Education and Rehabilitation Centers and Their Solutions
text_snippet: Problems Faced by Child Development Specialists Working in Special Education and Rehabilitation Centers and Their Solutions Introduction: It is well-documented that child development specialists face various problems while working in special education and rehabilitation centers, highlighting the need for research aimed at generating effective solutions. The present study aims to identify the problems experienced by child development specialists with bachelor's degrees working in special education and rehabilitation centers and to propose viable solutions to these problems. In line with this objective, interviews were conducted with 25 female participants from Karaman, Konya, and Ankara. Through these interviews, the specific issues faced by specialists were identified, and corresponding solution suggestions were offered.Method: The study was conducted with a case study within the scope of qualitative research. The participants of the study consisted of 25 child development specialists with bachelor's degrees working in special education and rehabilitation centers in Karaman, Konya and Ankara. Demographic information form and interview form were used as data collection tools in the study. title: Augmented Reality in Auditory-visual Conditional Discrimination Training for Children with Autism
text_snippet: Augmented Reality in Auditory-visual Conditional Discrimination Training for Children with Autism Introduction: Auditory-visual conditional discrimination is essential in developing functional skills, such as self-care and cognitive, social, and academic skills. Despite the availability of various effective methods, some children continue to face challenges in acquiring this form of discrimination.Method: This study compared the effectiveness and efficiency of using picture cards versus augmented reality as learning material for auditory-visual conditional discrimination in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Three boys aged 3 to 6, all diagnosed with ASD, participated in this study. Instruction and data collection took place in the participants’ homes. A single-subject research design was used, an adapted alternating treatment design embedded in multiple probes across participants.Findings: Results showed that all participants successfully acquired the skill under augmented reality conditions, generalized their learning to different instructional sets, and retained their skills for two and five weeks after instruction. title: I Speak, I Ask, I Learn: The Effectiveness of Teaching Question-Asking Through the Mand-Model Technique
text_snippet: I Speak, I Ask, I Learn: The Effectiveness of Teaching Question-Asking Through the Mand-Model Technique Introduction: It is known that when children with Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) between the ages of 24-36 months do not exhibit age-appropriate language development performance, they are described as having “delayed language and speech” (DLS). Children's act of asking questions is not only an indicator of interest, curiosity, desire to learn, and problem-solving skills, but also provides insight into their language abilities such as social communication, comprehension, and syntax. One of the various approaches used in therapies for language disorders is an intervention called Milieu Language Teaching techniques (Milieu Language Teaching). The study aims to determine the effectiveness of the Mand-Model (MM) technique, one of the milieu language teaching techniques, in teaching a child with DLD to ask questions such as “what is this”, “who is this” and “where is this”.Method: The multiple probe design across behaviors, one of the single-subject research methods, was used in this study investigating the effectiveness of the MM technique in teaching a child with DLD to ask the questions “what is this”, “who is this” and “where is this”. title: Emotion Regulation and Pragmatic Language Skills in Developmental Language Disorder and Typical Development
text_snippet: Emotion Regulation and Pragmatic Language Skills in Developmental Language Disorder and Typical Development Introduction: Developmental language disorder (DLD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects the learning, expression and comprehension of language. Children diagnosed with DLD may experience difficulties in peer relationships, display behavioral problems, or encounter challenges in social-emotional development due to inadequacies in their pragmatic language skills. This study aims to evaluate the emotion regulation and pragmatic language skills of 60- to 72-month-old children with DLD those with Typical Language Development (TLD), and to examine the relationship between these two skills.Method: Seventeen (1 girl; 16 boys) children diagnosed with DLD and 26 (15 girls, 11 boys) children with TLD aged 60-72 months were included in the study. Data were collected face-to-face using the “Participant Information Form”, “Preschool Emotion Regulation Scale (PERS)” and “Pragmatic Language Skills Inventory Turkish Version (PDBE-TV)”. The data were analyzed using IBM SPSS 27.0 for Windows.Findings: It was found that children diagnosed with TLD had lower performance in emotion regulation (p = .000) and pragmatic language skills (p = .000) compared to children with TLD. title: The Use of Technology in Classroom Management: A Systematic Review of Single-case Experimental Research
text_snippet: The Use of Technology in Classroom Management: A Systematic Review of Single-case Experimental Research Introduction: Teachers and researchers are a positive classroom climate. This study aims to examine the single-case experimental research on technology-based interventions used by teachers in general and special education classrooms for classroom management regarding their descriptive characteristics and methodological quality. Method: We descriptively analyzed 20 studies meeting the inclusion criteria of the current study and assessed their methodological rigor according to the What Works Clearinghouse (2020) design standards. Results: Descriptive findings revealed that technology-based interventions were effective in facilitating classroom management in classrooms with students with special educational needs and students with typical development. The findings regarding methodological rigor indicated that most of the research (n = 16) was at the desired level in terms of design standards. Discussion: Implications for further research and practice are discussed in line with the findings.

title: Investigation of Parents' Views on the Use of Sanitary Pads by Women with Special Needs
text_snippet: Investigation of Parents' Views on the Use of Sanitary Pads by Women with Special Needs Introduction: Evaluating the use of sanitary pads by women with special needs during menstruation and their parents' experiences is essential for understanding the needs of these individuals and their families. This study aimed to examine the views and experiences of parents regarding the use of sanitary pads by women with special needs. Method: This study used a phenomenological design, one of the qualitative research methods. The study group consisted of 10 volunteer parents with a daughter between the ages of 10 and 18 with special needs. The data were collected using a five-question semi-structured interview form developed with information obtained from the literature on the use of sanitary pads by women with special needs and the experiences of parents. The data were then interpreted using the content analysis technique.Findings: In the study, it was found that women with special needs faced problems of not being able to recognize menstruation periods, not being able to use sanitary pads, and exhibiting problem behaviors due to the physical and emotional changes they experienced during this period. title: Social Skills Development in Special Education: The Role of Religious Culture and Moral Knowledge Textbooks in Special Education
text_snippet: Social Skills Development in Special Education: The Role of Religious Culture and Moral Knowledge Textbooks in Special Education Introduction: This study aims to examine the potential of Religious Culture and Moral Education (RCME) textbooks to support the social skill development of students with special educational needs. Social skills constitute fundamental competencies that enable individuals to communicate effectively, sustain social relationships, and adapt to their environment. For students with special needs, it is critically important that these skills be reinforced through structured, concrete, and well-designed instructional processes.Method: The RCME textbooks used at the primary and lower secondary levels within the Ministry of National Education were analyzed through qualitative content analysis. Written content was systematically coded and categorized according to social skill themes, visual materials, activity samples, and explanatory texts.Findings: The analysis revealed that the textbooks include social skill themes such as empathy, tolerance, honesty, sharing, communication, and responsibility at varying levels of intensity. title: To What Extent Does Inclusive Education in Indonesia Achieve Equality for Dyslexic and Dysgraphia Students?
text_snippet: To What Extent Does Inclusive Education in Indonesia Achieve Equality for Dyslexic and Dysgraphia Students? Introduction: The implementation of inclusive education poses several challenges. Some of them involve a need for teacher resources and training, community, cultural, social, and cultural readiness, as well as other policies. Therefore, the active participation and empowerment of students with dyslexia and dysgraphia in inclusive schools in Indonesia is essential to build a fair educational environment. Substantially, this article will discuss the concept of educational inclusivity as a form of equal access for students with dyslexia and dysgraphia in Indonesia. Method: This study used a Systematic Literature Review (SLR). We used the Scopus and ScienceDirect databases. The study was carried out in compliance with PRISMA criteria.
